items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02
items.q: Yes, Pico, in that old time jazz. And I worked with him a lot, you know that.

ctx.x: I wondered about some of the clarinet players that you've played with. Who would be your favorite clarinet players in the old days, especially the older men that you remember when you were a boy? I like Pico.
Yes, Pico, in that old time jazz. And I worked with him a lot, you know that. Yes.
Did you ever work with Big Eye Louie?

items.title: De De Pierce Interview, 1960-01-10
items.q: Piku would run his band and let it live where he wanted, you know.

ctx.x: He would play the lead, so?

Oh yes indeed, the lead band was sure. He had a lot of work in it, because Piku would run his band and let it live where he wanted, you know. Fragile music like he wanted. Cut it up whatever he wanted to do. He had that part to do.

Now when you started out, say they'd have a six piece band, I'll just choose for example, trumpet, clarinet, trombone, and a bass, and a guitar, and drums. Now, how would you play a tune in those days? Would it be the full band at first, or would it be one man, or how would you start off?
